long_biography.plain_text:
When Craig Jackson took charge of Barrett-Jackson in 1995, he recognised that the collector-car audience was moving beyond the prewar classics favoured by his father's generation. He broadened the field to postwar performance cars and hot rods and made national television central to a more accessible automotive event.

Jackson had learned the business alongside his father, Russ, and older brother Brian, with hands-on experience in restoration as well as the auction itself. Under his leadership the Scottsdale sale developed into a multi-location collector-car platform. Charity remained part of that growth: Jackson established a cancer-research fund in memory of his father and brother, while charity vehicles became a recurring feature of Barrett-Jackson auctions.

uncertainties.detail: Craig Jackson is a common name, but the immutable American identity and 1959 birth year align with Forbes' age reporting, Jackson's first-person Pontiac birthplace account and a consistent Barrett-Jackson chain naming father Russ, brother Brian and co-founder Tom Barrett. This excludes unrelated Craig Jackson namesakes and resolves the subject as the second-generation auction executive.

The immutable record gives 2 September 1959. Forbes' age 53 in December 2012 independently corroborates the 1959 year, and Jackson directly identifies Pontiac as his birthplace, but the reviewed strong sources did not independently publish the exact day and month. The existing date is neither changed nor re-proposed.

Strong sources establish that Russ Jackson and Tom Barrett created the company, that Craig worked in the family operation and assumed leadership after his father and brother, and that he materially transformed its reach. They do not disclose probate or the precise transfer of shares. Inherited and expanded therefore describes the received operating platform and documented growth without claiming a particular legal transfer.

SEC evidence records IMG's purchase of 55 percent of Barrett-Jackson in 2022, and MARI announced Barrett-Jackson as part of its portfolio after acquiring the majority interest in 2025. Public sources do not disclose Craig Jackson's current personal percentage. The dossier therefore classifies him as Operator and does not call him the controlling owner or attribute the company's assets to him personally.

The existing Instagram account @craig_jackson427 is independently tied to the Barrett-Jackson chief executive by automotive media and company-linked promotion, so it is retained rather than re-proposed. Focused searches did not verify an exact personal LinkedIn, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, personal website, dedicated Wikipedia biography or Forbes profile. Only the official company website is proposed.

review.notes: Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] Auction executive: Jackson has led a major collector-car auction company since 1995 and remains its chairman and chief executive under outside majority ownership. [2] Automotive event promotion: Jackson expanded a single Scottsdale auction into televised, multi-day, multi-location automotive-lifestyle events, creating a durable live-event business model distinct from vehicle retail. [3] Automotive media: Jackson made national television and related automotive media central to Barrett-Jackson's transformation and audience growth. [4] Automotive restorer: Jackson gained hands-on vehicle-restoration experience in the family business, providing the technical grounding that later shaped his collector-car auction strategy. [5] Barrett-Jackson: Barrett-Jackson is Jackson's inherited-and-expanded family business, continuing employer and defining public association as chairman and chief executive. [6] Charity auctioning: Charity vehicles are a recurring, historically rooted feature of Barrett-Jackson auctions under Jackson, separate from his own cancer-research fund. [7] Collector-car auctions: Collector-car auctioning is the specific business through which Jackson inherited, expanded and continues to operate Barrett-Jackson, and is meaningfully narrower than the Automotive industry marker. [8] Jackson family (Barrett-Jackson): Russ Jackson co-founded the auction company, his son Brian led it, and Craig Jackson succeeded and expanded it, establishing a distinctive multigenerational automotive-auction family.
